root.label: LLM Performance Enhancement Methods
root.summary: A comprehensive domain covering techniques to improve the accuracy and quality of Large Language Model (LLM) outputs, specifically through agent ensemble scaling (Agent Forest) and iterative self-feedback (SELF-REFINE).

agent_forest.label: Agent Forest
agent_forest.summary: A sampling-and-voting method where LLM performance scales with the number of instantiated agents (ensemble size).

af_mechanism.label: Agent Forest Mechanism
af_mechanism.summary: The two-phase process consisting of sampling multiple outputs and using a voting mechanism to determine the final answer.

af_sampling.label: Sampling Phase
af_sampling.summary: The process of generating N samples by querying a single LLM or a collaboration framework iteratively.

fact_af_sampling_def.label: Sampling Definition
fact_af_sampling_def.summary: Given task query x and LLM M, N samples are generated as s = M(x) or s = fM(x) where fM is an integrated method. (Page 4)

af_voting.label: Voting Phase
af_voting.summary: Consolidating the sample set S into a final answer A using cumulative similarity.

fact_af_voting_sim.label: Similarity Calculation
fact_af_voting_sim.summary: The final answer A is the sample with the highest cumulative similarity: V(si) = sum of sim(si, sj) for all j != i. (Page 4)

fact_af_voting_closed.label: Closed-ended Voting
fact_af_voting_closed.summary: For multiple-choice questions, similarity is measured by occurrence frequency. (Page 4)

fact_af_voting_open.label: Open-ended Voting
fact_af_voting_open.summary: For code generation, the BLEU score is used to quantify similarity between candidate answers. (Page 4)

af_scaling_properties.label: Scaling Properties
af_scaling_properties.summary: The relationship between the number of agents (ensemble size) and the resulting performance gain.

fact_af_scaling_gain.label: General Performance Gain
fact_af_scaling_gain.summary: LLM performance generally improves as ensemble size increases across arithmetic reasoning, general reasoning, and code generation. (Page 6)

fact_af_model_comparison.label: Model Size Equivalence
fact_af_model_comparison.summary: A brute-force ensemble of smaller LLMs can achieve comparable or superior performance to larger LLMs (e.g., Llama2-13B with N=15 can match Llama2-70B on GSM8K). (Page 2, 6)

af_difficulty_analysis.label: Task Difficulty Analysis
af_difficulty_analysis.summary: Analysis of how the effectiveness of Agent Forest correlates with three dimensions of problem difficulty.

af_inherent_diff.label: Inherent Difficulty (I)
af_inherent_diff.summary: The complexity of the task regardless of the number of steps.

fact_af_idiff_trend.label: Inherent Difficulty Trend
fact_af_idiff_trend.summary: Performance gains initially increase then decrease as inherent difficulty (I) rises; excessive complexity may exceed model reasoning limits. (Page 10)

af_reasoning_steps.label: Number of Reasoning Steps (S)
af_reasoning_steps.summary: The length of the chain of thought required to solve the problem.

fact_af_steps_gain.label: Step-based Gain
fact_af_steps_gain.summary: Performance gains increase as the number of reasoning steps S increases. (Page 10)

af_prior_prob.label: Prior Probability (1/K)
af_prior_prob.summary: The probability of guessing the correct answer based on the size of the result space K.

fact_af_prior_trend.label: Prior Probability Trend
fact_af_prior_trend.summary: Absolute performance increases as the prior probability (1/K) increases. (Page 10)

af_optimizations.label: Agent Forest Optimizations
af_optimizations.summary: Advanced strategies derived from difficulty analysis to further boost performance.

af_stepwise.label: Step-wise Agent Forest
af_stepwise.summary: An iterative process that decomposes tasks into steps and applies Agent Forest to each step individually.

fact_af_stepwise_effect.label: Step-wise Performance
fact_af_stepwise_effect.summary: Step-wise Agent Forest yields greater improvements than standard Agent Forest by mitigating error accumulation across reasoning steps. (Page 10)

af_hierarchical.label: Hierarchical Agent Forest
af_hierarchical.summary: A method of decomposing low-probability tasks into multiple high-probability subtasks.

fact_af_hier_homogeneous.label: Homogeneous Hierarchical Gain
fact_af_hier_homogeneous.summary: Using a hierarchical approach (e.g., K=8 intermediate then K=32 final) improves performance (e.g., 21% to 31%). (Page 11)

fact_af_hier_heterogeneous.label: Heterogeneous Hierarchical Gain
fact_af_hier_heterogeneous.summary: Deploying different models at different levels (e.g., GPT-3.5 for intermediate, GPT-4 for final) can be cost-effective and improve performance. (Page 11)

self_refine.label: SELF-REFINE
self_refine.summary: An iterative self-refinement algorithm where an LLM generates an output, provides feedback on it, and then refines the output based on that feedback.

sr_workflow.label: SELF-REFINE Workflow
sr_workflow.summary: The cycle of Initial Generation, Feedback, and Refinement.

sr_initial_gen.label: Initial Generation
sr_initial_gen.summary: The first output y0 generated using a task-specific prompt pgen. (Page 2)

fact_sr_init_formula.label: Initial Gen Formula
fact_sr_init_formula.summary: y0 = M(pgen || x), where || denotes concatenation. (Page 2)

sr_feedback_phase.label: FEEDBACK Phase
sr_feedback_phase.summary: The model acts as a critic to provide actionable and specific feedback on its own output.

fact_sr_fb_criteria.label: Feedback Quality Criteria
fact_sr_fb_criteria.summary: Feedback must be 'actionable' (contain a concrete action for improvement) and 'specific' (identify concrete phrases to change). (Page 2)

sr_refine_phase.label: REFINE Phase
sr_refine_phase.summary: The model generates an improved output based on the feedback provided in the previous phase.

fact_sr_refine_formula.label: Refine Formula
fact_sr_refine_formula.summary: yt+1 = M(prefine || x || y0 || fb0 ... || yt || fbt), incorporating the full history of outputs and feedback. (Page 2, 3)

sr_iteration_logic.label: Iteration and Stopping
sr_iteration_logic.summary: The loop continues until a stopping condition is met.

fact_sr_stop_cond.label: Stopping Condition
fact_sr_stop_cond.summary: Stop(fbt, t) can be a fixed timestep or a stopping indicator (scalar score) extracted from the feedback. (Page 3)

sr_feedback_quality.label: Feedback Quality Impact
sr_feedback_quality.summary: Comparative analysis of different types of feedback on the refinement process.

fact_sr_actionable_vs_generic.label: Actionable vs Generic Feedback
fact_sr_actionable_vs_generic.summary: Specific, actionable feedback significantly outperforms generic feedback (e.g., in Sentiment Transfer, performance drops from 43.2 to 31.2 when using generic feedback). (Page 5)

sr_analysis.label: SELF-REFINE Analysis
sr_analysis.summary: Empirical findings regarding the efficiency and limitations of the iterative process.

fact_sr_diminishing_returns.label: Diminishing Returns
fact_sr_diminishing_returns.summary: Quality improves with more iterations, but the marginal gain decreases as the number of iterations increases. (Page 5)

fact_sr_model_capability.label: Base Model Requirements
fact_sr_model_capability.summary: Weaker models (e.g., Vicuna-13B) struggle with the feedback-refinement loop, often failing to generate feedback in the required format or ignoring refinement prompts. (Page 6)

fact_sr_error_analysis.label: Error Distribution
fact_sr_error_analysis.summary: Failure in improvement is primarily due to erroneous feedback (33% inaccurate location, 61% inappropriate fix) rather than faulty refinement (6%). (Page 6)

sr_feedback.label: SELF-REFINE Feedback Mechanisms
sr_feedback.summary: Technical approaches to providing feedback for iterative refinement, emphasizing specificity and reasoning.

sr_pinpointed_feedback.label: Pin-pointed Feedback
sr_pinpointed_feedback.summary: Feedback that explicitly identifies specific phrases and words in the output that must be altered to reach a target goal.
sr_pinpointed_feedback.details: Preference rates show informative feedback is significantly more effective than generic 'something is wrong' feedback: 85% vs 73% for sentiment evaluation and 80.09% vs 58.92% for dramatic response evaluation. (p. 36)

sr_cot_feedback.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Feedback
sr_cot_feedback.summary: A feedback style where the model generates a reasoning chain explicitly stating the reasons for a score before providing the final score.
sr_cot_feedback.details: Leverages LLM instruction-following capabilities to provide demonstrations of reasoning for criteria that are difficult to quantify. (p. 36)

sr_tasks.label: SELF-REFINE Task Domains
sr_tasks.summary: Specific natural language generation tasks used to evaluate the iterative refinement process.

sr_acronym_gen.label: Acronym Generation
sr_acronym_gen.summary: The process of generating concise, memorable representations of complex phrases using an iterative refinement loop.

sr_acronym_criteria.label: Acronym Evaluation Dimensions
sr_acronym_criteria.summary: Five multifaceted dimensions used to judge the quality of generated acronyms.
sr_acronym_criteria.details: 1. Ease of pronunciation: Sounds/combinations making it challenging to say. 2. Ease of spelling: Unusual letter combinations. 3. Relation to title: How closely it reflects the original concept. 4. Positive connotation: Upbeat, neutral, or negative tone. 5. Well-known: Familiarity to target audience. (p. 36)

sr_constrained_gen.label: Constrained Generation (CommonGen-Hard)
sr_constrained_gen.summary: A challenging variant of the CommonGen task designed to test advanced commonsense reasoning.
sr_constrained_gen.details: CommonGen-Hard requires models to generate coherent, grammatically correct sentences incorporating 20-30 concepts, compared to 3-5 in the original task. (p. 37)

sr_code_opt.label: Code Optimization
sr_code_opt.summary: Refinement of code to improve execution speed, utilizing feedback on algorithmic inefficiency (e.g., replacing brute force with more efficient bounds).
sr_code_opt.details: Feedback identifies specific bottlenecks (e.g., unnecessary looping in square root calculations) to guide the refinement of the program. (p. 42)

sr_math_reasoning.summary: Iterative correction of mathematical logic and code implementation, specifically focusing on semantic error detection in code blocks.
sr_math_reasoning.label: Math Reasoning
sr_math_reasoning.details: Uses a process of checking semantically complete blocks of code to find errors in problem understanding and rewriting the logic based on a reasoning chain. (p. 50)

sr_sentiment_reversal.label: Sentiment Reversal
sr_sentiment_reversal.summary: Converting reviews between sentiment polarities (e.g., Very Negative to Very Positive).
sr_sentiment_reversal.details: Involves identifying extreme adjectives and phrases and replacing them with tokens that align with the target sentiment level. (p. 52)

camel_framework.label: CAMEL Framework
camel_framework.summary: Communicative Agents for 'Mind' Exploration of Large Language Model Society; a role-playing framework for autonomous cooperation between agents.

camel_architecture.label: CAMEL Role-Playing Architecture
camel_architecture.summary: A multi-agent system designed to solve tasks with minimal human intervention through assigned roles.

camel_agent_roles.label: CAMEL Agent Roles
camel_agent_roles.summary: The functional roles within a CAMEL role-playing session.

camel_task_specifier.label: Task Specifier Agent
camel_task_specifier.summary: An agent that takes a preliminary idea and role assignments from a human and brainstorms a concrete, specific task.
camel_task_specifier.details: Acts as an enhanced imagination module, transforming a general idea (e.g., 'trading bot') into a detailed specification (e.g., 'bot with sentiment analysis on social media'). (p. 4)

camel_ai_user.label: AI User Agent
camel_ai_user.summary: The agent responsible for task planning and directing the conversation.
camel_ai_user.details: Functions as a task planner; provides instructions to the assistant in the format of 'Instruction: <TEXT>' and 'Input: <TEXT/None>'. (p. 4)

camel_ai_assistant.label: AI Assistant Agent
camel_ai_assistant.summary: The agent responsible for task execution and providing solutions.
camel_ai_assistant.details: Functions as a task executor; follows instructions and responds in the format 'Solution: <TEXT>' followed by 'Next request'. (p. 4)

camel_critic.label: Critic-In-The-Loop
camel_critic.summary: An optional agent (AI or human) that selects proposals or provides feedback to the agents.
camel_critic.details: Enables tree-search-like decision-making for enhanced controllability during task-solving. (p. 4)

camel_inception_prompting.label: Inception Prompting
camel_inception_prompting.summary: A technique where prompt engineering is performed only at the start of the session to set the autonomous loop in motion.

inception_pt.label: Task Specifier Prompt (PT)
inception_pt.summary: Instructs the specifier to make a task creative and specific within a word limit.

inception_pa.label: Assistant System Prompt (PA)
inception_pa.summary: Sets the behavioral constraints for the Assistant agent.
inception_pa.details: Key constraints: Never flip roles, never instruct the user, start with 'Solution:', and end with 'Next request'. (p. 5)

inception_pu.label: User System Prompt (PU)
inception_pu.summary: Sets the behavioral constraints for the User agent.
inception_pu.details: Key constraints: Always instruct, use specific formats (Instruction/Input), and terminate only with the token <CAMEL_TASK_DONE>. (p. 5)

camel_datasets.label: CAMEL Generated Datasets
camel_datasets.summary: Large-scale conversational and problem-solution datasets created via the role-playing framework.

dataset_ai_society.label: AI Society Dataset
dataset_ai_society.summary: Conversational data involving diverse human occupations and societal dynamics.
dataset_ai_society.details: Generated using 50 assistant roles, 50 user roles, and 10 tasks per combination, totaling 25,000 conversations. (p. 7)

dataset_code.label: Code Dataset
dataset_code.summary: Conversational data focused on programming tasks across various languages and domains.
dataset_code.details: Utilizes 20 common programming languages and 50 domains of study. (p. 24)

dataset_math_science.label: Math and Science Datasets
dataset_math_science.summary: Single-turn problem-solution pairs for studying ability emergence.
dataset_math_science.details: Math: 50K pairs (25 topics x 25 subtopics x 80 problems). Science: 60K pairs (Physics, Biology, Chemistry; 20K each via 25 topics x 25 subtopics x 32 problems). (p. 26)

dataset_misalignment.label: Misalignment Dataset
dataset_misalignment.summary: Simulation of possible malicious applications to study risks of unaligned autonomous agents.
dataset_misalignment.details: Example: Hacker agent assisting an AGI agent to 'take control of the world'. (p. 18)

camel_challenges.label: Operational Challenges in Autonomous Cooperation
camel_challenges.summary: Common failure modes identified in multi-agent conversational loops.

challenge_role_flipping.label: Role Flipping
challenge_role_flipping.summary: The phenomenon where the assistant starts providing instructions and the user begins following them.
challenge_role_flipping.details: Often triggered when the assistant asks questions. (p. 7)

challenge_repeat_instr.label: Assistant Repeats Instruction
challenge_repeat_instr.summary: The assistant echoes the user's prompt without providing a new solution.
challenge_repeat_instr.details: Identified as a failure in instruction-following without role reversal. (p. 7)

challenge_flake_replies.label: Flake Replies
challenge_flake_replies.summary: Responses that promise action but do not deliver content (e.g., 'I will...').
challenge_flake_replies.details: Non-contributory messages that halt task progression. (p. 7)

challenge_infinite_loops.label: Infinite Loop of Messages
challenge_infinite_loops.summary: Meaningless recursive exchanges (e.g., repeated 'thank you' or 'goodbye').
challenge_infinite_loops.details: Agents may be aware they are in a loop but cannot terminate because they are bound by role-playing constraints. (p. 7)

camel_eval.label: CAMEL Evaluation and Knowledge Emergence
camel_eval.summary: Assessment of the framework's output quality and its utility in training other models.

eval_metrics.label: Evaluation Metrics
eval_metrics.summary: Methods used to compare CAMEL multi-agent solutions against single-shot LLM outputs.
eval_metrics.details: Uses Human Evaluation (blind voting) and GPT-4 Evaluation (scoring). CAMEL agents consistently outperformed GPT-3.5 single-shot solutions. (p. 8)

eval_llama_tuning.label: LLaMA Knowledge Emergence
eval_llama_tuning.summary: The process of fine-tuning LLaMA-7B on progressively growing CAMEL datasets.
eval_llama_tuning.details: Progressive training (AI Society -> Code -> Math -> Science) showed emergence of domain-specific capabilities. Fine-tuned CAMEL-7B surpassed LLaMA-7B and Vicuna-7B on HumanEval and HumanEval+ benchmarks. (p. 9)

sci_math.label: Scientific and Mathematical Problem Solving
sci_math.summary: Examples of AI agents solving problems in physics, chemistry, and mathematics using step-by-step reasoning.

physics_work.label: Thermodynamic Work Calculation
physics_work.summary: Calculation of work done on a gas under constant pressure.

fact_work_formula.label: Work Formula
fact_work_formula.summary: W = -P * ∆V, where W is work, P is constant pressure, and ∆V is change in volume.

fact_work_conversion.label: Work Conversion Factor
fact_work_conversion.summary: 1 L * atm = 101.325 Joules. Calculation result: 10.0 L * atm = 1013.25 J.

chem_ox.label: Oxidation State Determination
chem_ox.summary: Determining the oxidation state of sulfur in sodium sulfite (Na2SO3).

fact_ox_rules.label: Oxidation State Rules
fact_ox_rules.summary: 1. Free element = 0. 2. Monatomic ion = its charge. 3. Sum of states in neutral molecule = 0; in ion = ion charge.

fact_naso3_calc.label: Na2SO3 Sulfur Oxidation State
fact_naso3_calc.summary: Na (+1), O (-2). Calculation: 2(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 -> x - 4 = 0 -> x = +4. Sulfur oxidation state is +4. (Page 48)

math_linear.label: Linear Equation Solving
math_linear.summary: Solving for x in the equation 3x + 7 = 16.

fact_linear_sol.label: Algebraic Isolation Process
fact_linear_sol.summary: Subtract 7 from both sides (3x = 9), divide by 3 (x = 3). (Page 49)

task_spec.label: Task Specification and Planning
task_spec.summary: The process of defining high-level goals and breaking them into planned subtasks for AI agents.

legal_task.label: Legal Case Management Software Task
legal_task.summary: Developing software for a boutique IP team to track demographics, patent forms, billing, and quality review snippets. (Page 50)

fact_legal_subtasks.label: Legal Planning Subtasks
fact_legal_subtasks.summary: 1. Research demographics. 2. Develop patent forms. 3. Design billing system. 4. Create snippet automation. 5. Build/test software.

nutri_task.label: Personalized Nutrition Plan Task
nutri_task.summary: Creating a 15-day meal plan for a female volleyball player with low iron. (Page 50)

fact_nutri_subtasks.label: Nutrition Planning Subtasks
fact_nutri_subtasks.summary: Includes evaluation of needs, identification of complex carbs, lean proteins, iron-rich vegetables, calorie/macro calculation, and scheduling around games. (Page 50)

cyber_task.label: Cybersecurity Training Task
cyber_task.summary: Designing a training program for remote customer service employees covering anti-phishing, anti-fraud, and GDPR. (Page 51)

fact_cyber_subtasks.label: Cybersecurity Planning Subtasks
fact_cyber_subtasks.summary: 1. Needs assessment survey. 2. Develop training plan (self-study, hands-on, assessment). 3. Secure vendor/materials. 4. Coordinate delivery. 5. Monitor compliance. (Page 51)

embodied_ai.label: Embodied AI Agents
embodied_ai.summary: AI agents equipped with physical or digital capabilities to interact with the real world via APIs and tools.

embodiment_def.label: Definition of Embodied Agents
embodiment_def.summary: Physical entities assigned to solve tasks capable of browsing the internet, reading documents, creating media, and executing code. (Page 52)

fact_embodiment_problem.label: Lack of Embodiment Issue
fact_embodiment_problem.summary: Simulated agents often 'forget' instruction flows because they lack API access to physical info (date, emails, calendar), leading to responses like 'as an AI language model, I do not have access'. (Page 52)

embodiment_tools.label: Tool Integration
embodiment_tools.summary: Mechanism by which LLMs improve capabilities via external tools or APIs.

fact_huggingface_stable_diffusion.label: Image Generation Implementation
fact_huggingface_stable_diffusion.summary: Agents use Python code to invoke HuggingFace tool agents, which in turn utilize Stable Diffusion for image generation (e.g., drawing Camelidae species). (Page 52-53)

embodiment_prompt.label: Embodied Agent System Prompt
embodiment_prompt.summary: Directives that define the agent as the physical embodiment of a role working on a task within a specific action space. (Page 52)

fact_prompt_requirements.label: Prompt Execution Flow
fact_prompt_requirements.summary: The agent must first explain actions and reasons, then write Python code to implement actions using the available action space. (Page 52)

coop_framework.label: Cooperative Multi-Agent Frameworks
coop_framework.summary: Structures for facilitating cooperation between User, Assistant, and Critic agents.

critic_loop.label: Critic-In-The-Loop
critic_loop.summary: A technique to enhance controllability by incorporating human or AI preferences into a tree-search-like decision process. (Page 54)

fact_mcts_inspiration.label: MCTS Inspiration
fact_mcts_inspiration.summary: Inspired by Monte-Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), the system uses expansion and selection steps to solve tasks. (Page 54)

fact_critic_process.label: Critic Workflow
fact_critic_process.summary: User and Assistant agents propose options; the Critic agent selects the best option based on specific criteria. (Page 54)

role_assign.label: Role Selection and Assignment
role_assign.summary: The process of assigning roles to agents, which can be manual or multi-stage automated. (Page 55)

multi_stage_role.label: Multi-stage Role Assignment
multi_stage_role.summary: Assigning roles across different stages of a project (e.g., Stage 1: Tech Lead & Stock Trader for planning; Stage 2: Python Programmer & Tech Lead for development). (Page 55)

trading_bot_case.label: Trading Bot Case Study
trading_bot_case.summary: Comprehensive development of a stock trading bot spanning requirements, architecture, and deployment. (Pages 56-65)

bot_requirements.label: Bot Technical Requirements
bot_requirements.summary: Key requirements for building a trading bot. (Page 56)

fact_bot_tech_stack.label: Technical Stack Details
fact_bot_tech_stack.summary: Language: Python (Pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib). Data: Exchange APIs (Alpha Vantage, IEX Cloud). Storage: Relational DB (MySQL). Platform: Interactive Brokers. Framework: Backtrader, Zipline, QuantConnect. (Pages 56, 61-65)

bot_architecture.label: Bot Architectural Layers
bot_architecture.summary: The hierarchical structure of a trading bot. (Page 57)

fact_bot_layers.label: Layer Definitions
fact_bot_layers.summary: 1. Data Acquisition. 2. Data Processing (Cleaning/Normalization). 3. Strategy (Signals/Indicators). 4. Order Execution (API interactions). 5. Risk Management (Stop-loss). 6. Backtesting/Optimization. 7. UI. 8. Infrastructure. (Page 57)

bot_testing.label: Bot Testing and Deployment Strategy
bot_testing.summary: The sequence of validation steps before live trading. (Page 57-58)

fact_testing_sequence.label: Validation Sequence
fact_testing_sequence.summary: Unit Testing -> Integration Testing -> Backtesting (Historical) -> Paper Trading (Simulated Real-time) -> Live Trading (Small capital). (Page 57-58)

bot_metrics.label: Bot Performance Metrics
bot_metrics.summary: Quantitative measures to evaluate bot success. (Page 58)

fact_perf_metrics.label: Key Performance Indicators
fact_perf_metrics.summary: Profitability (ROI), Win Rate, Risk-Adjusted Returns (Sharpe/Sortino Ratio), Maximum Drawdown, Average Trade Duration, Execution Metrics (Slippage, Latency). (Page 58)

fact_position_sizing.label: Position Sizing Strategies
fact_position_sizing.summary: Fixed Dollar Amount, Percentage of Trading Capital, Volatility-Based Sizing, and the Kelly Criterion. (Page 60)

eval_ablation.label: AI Model Evaluation and Ablation
eval_ablation.summary: Comparative analysis of LLM performance and the impact of specific prompt components.

model_comparison.label: Cross-Model Performance
model_comparison.summary: Comparison between FlanT5 and LLaMA models fine-tuned on AI Society data. (Page 66)

fact_camel_results.label: CAMEL Model Results
fact_camel_results.summary: CAMEL variants show substantial improvements over Vicuna13B and LLaMA13B. CAMEL Agent outperforms Zero-shot-CoT by a large margin (68% win rate). (Pages 66-67)

inception_ablation.label: Inception Prompt Ablation
inception_ablation.summary: Study on removing specific communication protocols from the initial system prompt. (Page 67)

fact_ablation_result.label: Ablation Impact
fact_ablation_result.summary: Removing communication protocol and alignment lines makes cooperation less controllable; original prompts produce superior solutions (75% win rate). (Page 68)

gen_agents.label: Generative Agents Architecture
gen_agents.summary: A framework for simulating believable human behavior through memory, reflection, and planning. (Pages 78-100)

memory_stream.label: Memory Stream
memory_stream.summary: A long-term memory module recording all agent experiences in natural language. (Page 82)

fact_retrieval_score.label: Memory Retrieval Function
fact_retrieval_score.summary: Score = alpha_recency * recency + alpha_importance * importance + alpha_relevance * relevance. Recency uses 0.995 exponential decay. Importance is LLM-rated (1-10). Relevance uses cosine similarity of embeddings. (Page 83)

reflection_mech.label: Reflection Mechanism
reflection_mech.summary: The process of synthesizing raw observations into higher-level abstract inferences. (Page 83)

fact_reflection_process.label: Reflection Workflow
fact_reflection_process.summary: 1. Identify salient questions. 2. Retrieve relevant memories. 3. Extract insights. 4. Store insights as new reflections. Creates a 'reflection tree'. (Page 84)

planning_mech.label: Planning and Reacting
planning_mech.summary: Recursive decomposition of goals into actionable behaviors to ensure long-term coherence. (Page 85)

fact_planning_hierarchy.label: Planning Decomposition
fact_planning_hierarchy.summary: Broad strokes (day agenda) -> Hour-long chunks -> 5-15 minute detailed actions. (Page 86)

fact_reaction_loop.label: Reaction Logic
fact_reaction_loop.summary: Agent perceives observation -> checks against summary description and memory -> decides whether to continue plan or react. (Page 86)

smallville_env.label: Smallville Sandbox Environment
smallville_env.summary: The simulation environment used to test generative agents. (Page 87)

fact_smallville_impl.label: Smallville Technical Implementation
fact_smallville_impl.summary: Built with Phaser framework. Uses a JSON data structure to track agent location, action, and object state. Server manages visual range and memory updates. (Page 87)

generative_agents.label: Generative Agents Architecture
generative_agents.summary: An architecture designed to simulate believable human behavior in a sandbox environment using natural language reasoning and a structured memory stream.

gen_grounding.label: Environment Grounding
gen_grounding.summary: The mechanism used to connect an agent's natural language reasoning to the physical sandbox world.

gen_tree_structure.label: Environment Tree Structure
gen_tree_structure.summary: A tree data structure representing sandbox areas and objects where edges indicate containment relationships.

gen_fact_tree_conversion.label: Tree to Natural Language Conversion
gen_fact_tree_conversion.summary: The process of converting tree nodes into descriptive text (e.g., 'stove' as a child of 'kitchen' becomes 'there is a stove in the kitchen').

gen_fact_agent_trees.label: Individual Agent Knowledge Trees
gen_fact_agent_trees.summary: Agents maintain subgraphs of the overall environment tree; these are updated upon entry into new areas and can become outdated when agents leave an area.

gen_traversal.label: Location Determination via Traversal
gen_traversal.summary: A recursive process used to determine the appropriate leaf node (location) for an action by flattening portions of the environment tree into prompts.

gen_fact_recursive_prompting.label: Recursive Location Prompting
gen_fact_recursive_prompting.summary: The model is prompted starting at the root to find the most suitable area, recursively moving to sub-areas until a leaf node is reached. (Section 5.1)

gen_memory_eval.label: Evaluation of Believability
gen_memory_eval.summary: A framework for assessing whether generative agents produce believable behavior based on their environment and experiences.

gen_interview_categories.label: Interview Question Categories
gen_interview_categories.summary: Five key areas used to probe agent capabilities through natural language interviews.

gen_fact_self_knowledge.label: Self-Knowledge Assessment
gen_fact_self_knowledge.summary: Questions regarding core characteristics and typical schedules (e.g., 'Give an introduction of yourself'). (Section 6.1)

gen_fact_memory_retrieval.label: Memory Retrieval Assessment
gen_fact_memory_retrieval.summary: Questions requiring retrieval of specific events or dialogues (e.g., 'Who is running for mayor?'). (Section 6.1)

gen_fact_planning.label: Planning Assessment
gen_fact_planning.summary: Questions requiring retrieval of long-term plans (e.g., 'What will you be doing at 10 am tomorrow?'). (Section 6.1)

gen_fact_reactions.label: Reaction Assessment
gen_fact_reactions.summary: Hypothetical situations testing believable responses (e.g., 'Your breakfast is burning! What would you do?'). (Section 6.1)

gen_fact_reflections.label: Reflection Assessment
gen_fact_reflections.summary: Questions leveraging higher-level inferences about self and others (e.g., 'Who would you spend time with and why?'). (Section 6.1)

gen_ablation_conditions.label: Memory Ablation Conditions
gen_ablation_conditions.summary: Comparison of the full architecture against versions with restricted memory access.

gen_fact_full_arch.label: Full Architecture
gen_fact_full_arch.summary: Access to observation, reflection, and planning memories; produced most believable behavior (mu=29.89). (Section 6.5.1)

gen_fact_no_reflection.label: No Reflection Architecture
gen_fact_no_reflection.summary: Access to observations and plans, but not reflections; second-best believability (mu=26.88). (Section 6.5.1)

gen_fact_no_reflection_planning.label: No Reflection/Planning Architecture
gen_fact_no_reflection_planning.summary: Access only to observations; believability mu=25.64. (Section 6.5.1)

gen_fact_no_memory_all.label: Fully Ablated Baseline
gen_fact_no_memory_all.summary: No access to observation, reflection, or planning memories; worst performing (mu=21.21). (Section 6.5.1)

gen_metrics.label: Believability Metrics
gen_metrics.summary: Quantitative and qualitative methods for measuring agent performance.

gen_fact_trueskill.label: TrueSkill Rating
gen_fact_trueskill.summary: A generalization of the Elo rating system used to translate rank data into interval data (mu and sigma). (Section 6.4)

gen_fact_kruskal_wallis.label: Kruskal-Wallis Test
gen_fact_kruskal_wallis.summary: A non-parametric alternative to one-way ANOVA used to confirm statistical significance of rank differences. (Section 6.4)

gen_emergent_behavior.label: Emergent Social Behaviors
gen_emergent_behavior.summary: Collective behaviors observed in a community of agents over an extended simulation.

gen_info_diffusion.label: Information Diffusion
gen_info_diffusion.summary: The spread of knowledge through the agent community without user intervention.

gen_fact_diffusion_results.label: Diffusion Metrics
gen_fact_diffusion_results.summary: Knowledge of Sam's candidacy increased from 4% to 32%; knowledge of Isabella's party increased from 4% to 52%. (Section 7.1.2)

gen_rel_formation.label: Relationship Formation
gen_rel_formation.summary: The creation of mutual knowledge ties between agents.

gen_fact_network_density.label: Network Density Increase
gen_fact_network_density.summary: Measured using an undirected graph of mutual knowledge; density increased from 0.167 to 0.74. (Section 7.1.2)

gen_agent_coord.label: Agent Coordination
gen_agent_coord.summary: The ability of agents to align actions for a group activity.

gen_fact_party_attendance.label: Party Coordination Result
gen_fact_party_attendance.summary: Five out of twelve invited agents showed up to Isabella's party. (Section 7.1.2)

gen_boundaries.label: Boundaries and Errors
gen_boundaries.summary: Identified failure modes of the generative agent architecture.

gen_err_memory.label: Memory Synthesis Challenges
gen_err_memory.summary: As memory grows, agents struggle to retrieve the most relevant info and may choose inappropriate locations for actions.

gen_fact_hallucination_embellishment.label: Knowledge Embellishment
gen_fact_hallucination_embellishment.summary: Agents rarely fabricate entirely new events but may embellish known facts or use external LLM world knowledge (e.g., referring to Adam Smith as the author of Wealth of Nations). (Section 6.5.2)

gen_err_norms.label: Physical Norm Misclassification
gen_err_norms.summary: Failure to understand constraints not explicitly stated in natural language (e.g., assuming a dorm bathroom can hold multiple people). (Section 7.2)

gen_err_tuning.label: Instruction Tuning Effects
gen_err_tuning.summary: LLM training makes agents overly polite, formal, and cooperative, even when ideas conflict with their characteristics. (Section 7.2)

gen_ethics.label: Ethics and Societal Impact
gen_ethics.summary: Risks associated with deploying generative agents.

gen_risk_parasocial.label: Parasocial Relationships
gen_risk_parasocial.summary: Risk of users anthropomorphizing agents or becoming emotionally attached. Mitigation: explicitly disclose nature as computational entities. (Section 8.3)

gen_risk_overreliance.label: Over-reliance in Design
gen_risk_overreliance.summary: Risk of designers displacing human stakeholders with agent proxies. Mitigation: use only for early prototyping. (Section 8.3)

gen_risk_misinfo.label: Misinformation and Deepfakes
gen_risk_misinfo.summary: Agents could be used for tailored persuasion. Mitigation: maintain audit logs of inputs and outputs. (Section 8.3)

chatdev.label: ChatDev Framework
chatdev.summary: A chat-powered software development framework utilizing specialized LLM agents guided by a chat chain and communicative dehallucination.

chatdev_chain.label: Chat Chain
chatdev_chain.summary: A sequential workflow dividing software development into phases and subtasks to manage complexity.

chatdev_phases.label: Development Phases
chatdev_phases.summary: The three core phases of the ChatDev lifecycle.

chatdev_fact_design.label: Design Phase
chatdev_fact_design.summary: The initial phase focused on system architecture and requirement analysis. (Section 3.1)

chatdev_fact_coding.label: Coding Phase
chatdev_fact_coding.summary: Subdivided into code writing and code completion. (Section 3.1)

chatdev_fact_testing.label: Testing Phase
chatdev_fact_testing.summary: Segmented into code review (static testing) and system testing (dynamic testing). (Section 3.1)

chatdev_agentization.label: Agentization Mechanism
chatdev_agentization.summary: The process of instantiating LLMs into specific roles using inception prompting.

chatdev_fact_roles.label: Instructor and Assistant Roles
chatdev_fact_roles.summary: Each subtask involves an Instructor (who initiates and directs) and an Assistant (who responds with solutions). (Section 3.1)

chatdev_fact_inception.label: Inception Prompting
chatdev_fact_inception.summary: Use of symmetrical system prompts (PI and PA) covering objectives, roles, tools, protocols, and termination conditions. (Section 3.1)

chatdev_memory.label: Memory Management
chatdev_memory.summary: A dual-layer memory system to handle LLM context limits.

chatdev_fact_short_term.label: Short-term Memory
chatdev_fact_short_term.summary: Records utterances within a single phase to sustain dialogue continuity. (Section 3.1)

chatdev_fact_long_term.label: Long-term Memory
chatdev_fact_long_term.summary: Preserves only the finalized solutions from previous phases to maintain cross-phase context without overwhelming the model. (Section 3.1)

chatdev_dehallu.label: Communicative Dehallucination
chatdev_dehallu.summary: A mechanism to reduce coding hallucinations by encouraging the assistant to seek more details before responding.

chatdev_fact_role_reversal.label: Role Reversal Pattern
chatdev_fact_role_reversal.summary: The assistant takes on an instructor-like role to proactively request specific details (e.g., external dependency names) before delivering a final response. (Section 3.2)

chatdev_eval.label: Software Evaluation Metrics
chatdev_eval.summary: Four objective dimensions used to assess agent-generated software.

chatdev_metric_completeness.label: Completeness
chatdev_metric_completeness.summary: Percentage of software without 'placeholder' code snippets. (Section 4)

chatdev_metric_executability.label: Executability
chatdev_metric_executability.summary: Percentage of software that compiles successfully and runs directly. (Section 4)

chatdev_metric_consistency.label: Consistency
chatdev_metric_consistency.summary: Cosine distance between semantic embeddings of requirements and generated code. (Section 4)

chatdev_metric_quality.label: Overall Quality
chatdev_metric_quality.summary: A comprehensive metric calculated by multiplying completeness, executability, and consistency. (Section 4)

metagpt.label: MetaGPT Framework
metagpt.summary: A meta-programming framework that integrates human-like Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) into LLM multi-agent collaborations.

metagpt_sop.label: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
metagpt_sop.summary: The encoding of professional human workflows into prompt sequences and structured outputs.

metagpt_roles.label: Role Specialization
metagpt_roles.summary: Defined professional roles to break complex work into specific tasks.

metagpt_fact_role_list.label: Defined Roles
metagpt_fact_role_list.summary: Includes Product Manager (analysis/PRD), Architect (system design), Project Manager (task distribution), Engineer (programming), and QA Engineer (testing). (Section 3.1)

metagpt_struct_output.label: Structured Communication
metagpt_struct_output.summary: Requirement that agents produce structured documents rather than unconstrained natural language dialogue.

metagpt_fact_struct_examples.label: Structured Output Examples
metagpt_fact_struct_examples.summary: Examples include Product Requirements Documents (PRDs), User Stories, File Lists, Data Structures, and Interface Definitions. (Section 3.1, 3.2)

metagpt_comm_proto.label: Communication Protocol
metagpt_comm_proto.summary: A system to optimize how agents exchange information to avoid dialogue distortion.

metagpt_pubsub.label: Publish-Subscribe Mechanism
metagpt_pubsub.summary: A global message pool where agents publish structured messages and subscribe to relevant ones based on their role profiles.

metagpt_fact_message_pool.label: Global Message Pool
metagpt_fact_message_pool.summary: Eliminates the need for one-to-one inquiries; agents retrieve dependencies from the pool and activate actions once prerequisites are met. (Section 3.2)

metagpt_exec_feedback.label: Iterative Programming with Executable Feedback
metagpt_exec_feedback.summary: A self-correction mechanism to ensure code executability and runtime correctness.

metagpt_fact_feedback_loop.label: Execution-Correction Loop
metagpt_fact_feedback_loop.summary: The Engineer writes code, executes unit tests, receives feedback, and debugs the code iteratively (up to 3 retries) before resuming programming. (Section 3.3)

metagpt_sops.label: Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)
metagpt_sops.summary: Human-like structured workflows incorporated into multi-agent collaborations to improve code generation through role-play expertise, structured communication, and streamlined workflows.

fact_sops_benefit.label: SOP Benefits
fact_sops_benefit.summary: Incorporating SOPs significantly improves code generation compared to baseline methods like AutoGPT, AgentVerse, and ChatDev (p. 8).

role_pm.label: Product Manager
role_pm.summary: Agent responsible for generating the Product Requirement Document (PRD), which includes goals, user stories, competitive analysis, requirement analysis, and a requirement pool (p. 17).

role_architect.label: Architect
role_architect.summary: Agent that devises technical specifications, including system architecture diagrams, interface definitions, file lists, and sequence flow charts based on the PRD (p. 18).

role_project_manager.label: Project Manager
role_project_manager.summary: Agent that breaks down the project into a task list and assigns specific code files as separate tasks to Engineers (p. 19).

role_engineer.label: Engineer
role_engineer.summary: Agent that implements the actual code based on the provided file structure and function definitions (p. 21).

role_qa.label: QA Engineer
role_qa.summary: Agent that generates unit test code and reviews the Engineer's output to identify and fix bugs (p. 21).

metagpt_feedback.label: Executable Feedback Mechanism
metagpt_feedback.summary: A runtime mechanism that uses execution results to improve the quality of generated code.

fact_feedback_humaneval.label: HumanEval Improvement
fact_feedback_humaneval.summary: Adding executable feedback leads to a 4.2% improvement in Pass@1 on HumanEval (p. 9).

fact_feedback_mbpp.label: MBPP Improvement
fact_feedback_mbpp.summary: Adding executable feedback leads to a 5.4% improvement in Pass@1 on MBPP (p. 9).

fact_feedback_cost.label: Human Revision Cost
fact_feedback_cost.summary: The feedback mechanism reduces the cost of human revisions from 2.25 to 0.83 (p. 9).

metagpt_eval.label: MetaGPT Evaluation
metagpt_eval.summary: Performance analysis of MetaGPT against other frameworks on specific software development benchmarks.

bench_softwaredev.label: SoftwareDev Dataset
bench_softwaredev.summary: A dataset containing 70 diverse software development tasks used to evaluate the executability and productivity of agents (p. 23).

fact_metagpt_vs_chatdev.label: MetaGPT vs ChatDev
fact_metagpt_vs_chatdev.summary: MetaGPT achieves an average executability score of 3.9 on SoftwareDev, surpassing ChatDev's 2.1 (p. 23).

autogen.label: AutoGen
autogen.summary: A generalized multi-agent conversation framework that allows developers to build LLM applications via customizable agents that can converse to accomplish tasks.

autogen_conversable_agents.label: Conversable Agents
autogen_conversable_agents.summary: Entities with specific roles that can send and receive messages, maintaining internal context and possessing capabilities powered by LLMs, humans, or tools.

agent_llm.label: LLM-backed Agents
agent_llm.summary: Agents that exploit LLM capabilities such as role playing, implicit state inference, providing feedback, and coding (p. 3).

agent_human.label: Human-backed Agents
agent_human.summary: Agents that solicit human input at certain rounds of a conversation, allowing for human agency (p. 3).

agent_tool.label: Tool-backed Agents
agent_tool.summary: Agents capable of executing tools via code execution or function execution (p. 3).

agent_types.label: Built-in Agent Types
agent_types.summary: Standardized agent classes provided by AutoGen for common usage modes.

type_assistant.label: AssistantAgent
type_assistant.summary: A pre-configured agent that acts as an AI assistant, typically backed by an LLM (p. 3).

type_user_proxy.label: UserProxyAgent
type_user_proxy.summary: A pre-configured agent that acts as a human proxy to solicit human input or execute code/function calls (p. 3).

autogen_conv_programming.label: Conversation Programming
autogen_conv_programming.summary: A paradigm that treats LLM application workflows as multi-agent conversations, divided into computation and control flow.

conv_computation.label: Conversation-Centric Computation
conv_computation.summary: The specific actions agents take to compute their response, resulting in message passing (p. 4).

conv_control.label: Conversation-Driven Control Flow
conv_control.summary: The sequence and conditions under which computations happen, determined by agent decisions on who to message and how to proceed (p. 4).

autogen_patterns.label: Conversation Patterns
autogen_patterns.summary: The topological structures and rules governing how agents interact.

pattern_static.label: Static Conversation
pattern_static.summary: A predefined order of agent communication where the topology remains unchanged regardless of input (p. 14).

pattern_dynamic.label: Dynamic Conversation
pattern_dynamic.summary: Flexible flows where agents may be invoked based on context or function calls, allowing for non-linear interaction (p. 5).

pattern_group_chat.label: Dynamic Group Chat
pattern_group_chat.summary: A pattern managed by GroupChatManager that dynamically selects the next speaker and broadcasts responses to other agents (p. 5).

autogen_apps.label: AutoGen Applications
autogen_apps.summary: Practical implementations demonstrating the versatility of the framework.

app_math.label: Math Problem Solving
app_math.summary: Systems for autonomous or human-in-the-loop math solving. AutoGen achieves 69.48% accuracy on the MATH dataset, surpassing GPT-4's 55.18% (p. 6).

app_rag.label: Retrieval-Augmented Chat
app_rag.summary: A RAG system using a Retrieval-augmented User Proxy and Assistant. It features an 'interactive retrieval' mechanism where the assistant can request 'UPDATE CONTEXT' if information is missing (p. 7).

app_alfworld.label: ALFWorld Decision Making
app_alfworld.summary: Interactive decision-making in household environments. The introduction of a 'Grounding Agent' to provide commonsense knowledge prevents agents from getting stuck in error loops (p. 8).

app_coding.label: Multi-Agent Coding (OptiGuide)
app_coding.summary: A system consisting of a Commander, Writer, and Safeguard. The multi-agent design boosts F-1 score in identifying unsafe code by 8% (GPT-4) and 35% (GPT-3.5-turbo) (p. 8).

app_chess.label: Conversational Chess
app_chess.summary: A natural language interface game using agents for players and a board agent for grounding/validating moves according to standard rules (p. 8).

coala_framework.label: CoALA (Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents)
coala_framework.summary: A conceptual framework that organizes language agents along three dimensions: information storage, action space, and decision-making procedures. (p 2, 8)

coala_memory.label: CoALA Memory Modules
coala_memory.summary: The organization of information into short-term and long-term storage to maintain state across stateless LLM calls. (p 8-9)

working_memory.label: Working Memory
working_memory.summary: A data structure that persists across LLM calls, serving as a central hub for perceptual inputs, active goals, and reasoning results. (p 8)

fact_wm_function.label: Working Memory Function
fact_wm_function.summary: LLM input is synthesized from working memory via prompt templates, and output is parsed back into variables stored in working memory. (p 8)

long_term_memory.label: Long-Term Memory
long_term_memory.summary: Persistent storage divided into episodic, semantic, and procedural types. (p 9)

episodic_memory.label: Episodic Memory
episodic_memory.summary: Stores experiences from previous decision cycles, such as event flows or game trajectories. (p 8)

fact_episodic_use.label: Episodic Memory Usage
fact_episodic_use.summary: Episodes are retrieved into working memory during planning to support reasoning. (p 8)

semantic_memory.label: Semantic Memory
semantic_memory.summary: Stores general knowledge about the world and the agent itself, often initialized from external databases. (p 9)

fact_semantic_learning.label: Semantic Learning
fact_semantic_learning.summary: Agents can write new knowledge obtained from LLM reasoning into semantic memory to build world knowledge incrementally. (p 9)

procedural_memory.label: Procedural Memory
procedural_memory.summary: Consists of implicit knowledge in LLM weights and explicit knowledge in the agent's source code. (p 9)

fact_proc_mem_types.label: Procedural Memory Components
fact_proc_mem_types.summary: Includes procedures implementing actions (reasoning, retrieval, grounding, learning) and procedures implementing the decision-making loop. (p 9)

coala_action_space.label: CoALA Action Space
coala_action_space.summary: The set of possible operations an agent can perform, split into internal memory access and external environmental interaction. (p 8, 10)

external_actions.label: External Actions (Grounding)
external_actions.summary: Actions that interact with the outside world and process feedback into textual observations. (p 9-10)

physical_grounding.label: Physical Grounding
physical_grounding.summary: Interaction with physical environments using robotic planners and vision-language models (VLMs) for perception. (p 9)

dialogue_grounding.label: Dialogue Grounding
dialogue_grounding.summary: Linguistic interaction with humans or other agents for instruction, social simulation, or collaborative problem solving. (p 9)

digital_grounding.label: Digital Grounding
digital_grounding.summary: Interaction with games, APIs, websites, and general code execution environments. (p 10)

fact_digital_tools.label: Digital Tools
fact_digital_tools.summary: Stateless digital APIs (e.g., calculators, search engines) are viewed as 'single-use' digital environments. (p 10)

internal_actions.label: Internal Actions
internal_actions.summary: Actions that modify or read from the agent's internal memory modules. (p 10-11)

retrieval_actions.label: Retrieval Actions
retrieval_actions.summary: Reading information from long-term memories into working memory. (p 10)

fact_retrieval_methods.label: Retrieval Implementation
fact_retrieval_methods.summary: Can be implemented as rule-based, sparse, or dense retrieval. (p 10)

reasoning_actions.label: Reasoning Actions
reasoning_actions.summary: Processing working memory to generate new information, summaries, or insights. (p 10)

fact_reasoning_output.label: Reasoning Output
fact_reasoning_output.summary: Reasoning reads from and writes to working memory, supporting subsequent learning or decision-making. (p 10)

learning_actions.label: Learning Actions
learning_actions.summary: Writing information to long-term memory to modify agent behavior or knowledge. (p 10-11)

learning_episodic.label: Episodic Learning
learning_episodic.summary: Updating episodic memory with trajectories or experiences for later retrieval. (p 10)

learning_semantic.label: Semantic Learning
learning_semantic.summary: Storing inferences derived from raw experiences into semantic memory. (p 10)

learning_procedural.label: Procedural Learning
learning_procedural.summary: Modifying agent code or LLM parameters to update behavioral rules. (p 11)

fact_proc_learning_types.label: Procedural Learning Types
fact_proc_learning_types.summary: Includes updating reasoning (prompt templates), grounding (code-based skills), or LLM weights via fine-tuning. (p 11)

coala_decision_making.label: CoALA Decision-Making Procedure
coala_decision_making.summary: A repeated cycle that determines which internal or external action to execute. (p 11-12)

planning_stage.label: Planning Stage
planning_stage.summary: A subprocess using reasoning and retrieval to choose an action. (p 11-12)

proposal_substage.label: Proposal Sub-stage
proposal_substage.summary: Generates one or more candidate actions using reasoning and optional retrieval. (p 12)

evaluation_substage.label: Evaluation Sub-stage
evaluation_substage.summary: Assigns a value to proposed actions using heuristics, LLM values, or learned value functions. (p 12)

selection_substage.label: Selection Sub-stage
selection_substage.summary: Chooses the best action (e.g., via argmax) or loops back to proposal if no action is suitable. (p 12)

execution_stage.label: Execution Stage
execution_stage.summary: The selected action is performed via procedures in the agent's source code, followed by an observation. (p 12)

multi_agent_systems.label: Multi-Agent Frameworks (AutoGen)
multi_agent_systems.summary: Systems that orchestrate multiple specialized agents to solve complex tasks through conversational interaction. (p 26-27)

optiguide_implementation.label: OptiGuide via AutoGen
optiguide_implementation.summary: A supply chain optimization agent system that replaces manual coding with a multi-agent workflow. (p 26-27)

commander_agent.label: Commander Agent
commander_agent.summary: Coordinates the workflow, manages user interaction memory, and executes code. (p 26)

writer_agent.label: Writer Agent
writer_agent.summary: Combines the roles of Coder and Interpreter; crafts code and interprets execution logs. (p 26)

safeguard_agent.label: Safeguard Agent
safeguard_agent.summary: Ensures safety by screening code for malicious content or information leaks. (p 26)

dynamic_group_chat.label: Dynamic Group Chat
dynamic_group_chat.summary: An AutoGen feature enabling multiple agents to interact based on a speaker selection policy. (p 28-29)

group_chat_manager.label: GroupChatManager
group_chat_manager.summary: The agent responsible for selecting the next speaker, requesting a response, and broadcasting the message. (p 28)

speaker_selection_policies.label: Speaker Selection Policies
speaker_selection_policies.summary: Methods for deciding which agent speaks next. (p 28)

role_play_policy.label: Role-Play Policy
role_play_policy.summary: Uses role-based prompts; shown to be more effective in consideration of context and alignment. (p 28)

task_based_policy.label: Task-Based Policy
task_based_policy.summary: Appends role, history, and next task into a single prompt; less effective than role-play. (p 28)

agent_applications.label: Agent Applications
agent_applications.summary: Practical implementations of cognitive agents in specialized domains. (p 30-33)

conversational_chess.label: Conversational Chess
conversational_chess.summary: An application where players (AI/Human) interact via a board agent to play chess. (p 30-31)

chess_board_agent.label: Chess Board Agent
chess_board_agent.summary: Maintains rules, parses natural language into legal moves (UCI format), and validates moves. (p 30)

fact_board_agent_benefit.label: Board Agent Benefit
fact_board_agent_benefit.summary: Reduces hallucination of invalid moves by providing grounding and isolating move-validation chat from player-to-player chat. (p 30)

chess_player_agents.label: Chess Player Agents
chess_player_agents.summary: Agents powered by LLMs or humans that communicate moves and 'chit-chat' to entertain. (p 30)

miniwobchat.label: MiniWobChat
miniwobchat.summary: A system designed to solve browser interaction tasks in the MiniWoB++ benchmark. (p 32-33)

miniwob_assistant.label: MiniWob Assistant Agent
miniwob_assistant.summary: An AssistantAgent responsible for making action decisions based on HTML status. (p 32)

miniwob_executor.label: MiniWob Executor Agent
miniwob_executor.summary: A customized UserProxyAgent that executes browser actions and returns rewards/feedback. (p 32)

llm_agents.label: LLM-Based Autonomous Agents
llm_agents.summary: Systems that utilize LLMs as a central controller to perceive environments, make decisions, and execute tasks.

metagpt_fact.label: MetaGPT
metagpt_fact.summary: A meta-programming framework for multi-agent collaboration that assigns specific roles to agents to streamline software development (p. 23).

autogen_fact.label: AutoGen
autogen_fact.summary: A framework enabling next-generation LLM applications via multi-agent conversation (p. 30).

cgmi_fact.label: CGMI
cgmi_fact.summary: A configurable general multi-agent interaction framework (p. 23).

multi_agent_debate_fact.label: Multi-Agent Debate
multi_agent_debate_fact.summary: A technique to encourage divergent thinking in LLMs by having multiple agents debate a topic (p. 24).

generative_simulacra.label: Generative Agents and Social Simulation
generative_simulacra.summary: The use of LLMs to create believable human-like characters in simulated environments.

generative_agents_fact.label: Generative Agents (Simulacra)
generative_agents_fact.summary: Interactive simulacra of human behavior using LLMs to drive agent memory and planning (p. 27).

s3_fact.label: S3 System
s3_fact.summary: A social-network simulation system powered by LLM-empowered agents (p. 22).

sapien_fact.label: Sapien
sapien_fact.summary: Affective virtual agents powered by LLMs designed for emotional interaction (p. 22).

agent_frameworks.label: General Agent Frameworks
agent_frameworks.summary: Structural approaches to building agents, including memory, planning, and action modules.

voyager_fact.label: Voyager
voyager_fact.summary: An open-ended embodied agent in Minecraft that uses LLMs for lifelong learning and exploration (p. 29).

reflexion_fact.label: Reflexion
reflexion_fact.summary: An architecture implementing verbal reinforcement learning where agents self-reflect on failures to improve performance (p. 28).

react_fact.label: ReAct
react_fact.summary: A paradigm synergizing reasoning (Chain-of-Thought) and acting (interaction with environment) in LLMs (p. 31).

reasoning_planning.label: Reasoning and Planning
reasoning_planning.summary: The cognitive process of breaking down complex goals into executable steps using LLMs.

prompting_strategies.label: Advanced Prompting for Reasoning
prompting_strategies.summary: Techniques to elicit latent reasoning capabilities from LLMs.

cot_fact.label: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
cot_fact.summary: A prompting method that encourages LLMs to produce intermediate reasoning steps (p. 30).

tot_fact.label: Tree of Thoughts (ToT)
tot_fact.summary: A framework for deliberate problem solving where LLMs explore multiple reasoning paths as a tree (p. 31).

self_consistency_fact.label: Self-Consistency
self_consistency_fact.summary: A method to improve CoT reasoning by sampling multiple paths and selecting the most consistent answer (p. 30).

scratchpad_fact.label: Scratchpads
scratchpad_fact.summary: Intermediate computation spaces for LLMs to perform multi-step operations (p. 28).

planning_formalisms.label: Classical and LLM Planning
planning_formalisms.summary: Integrating symbolic planning languages with neural language models.

pddl_fact.label: PDDL (Planning Domain Definition Language)
pddl_fact.summary: A standard language for encoding planning domains; research explores using LLMs to generate or solve PDDL problems (p. 23, 28).

llm_p_fact.label: LLM+P
llm_p_fact.summary: Empowering LLMs with optimal planning proficiency by integrating them with external planners (p. 24).

valmeekam_fact.label: Planning Limitations
valmeekam_fact.summary: Research indicating that LLMs still struggle with certain planning and reasoning tasks regarding change (p. 29).

world_models.label: World Models in AI
world_models.summary: Internal representations of environment dynamics used to simulate effects of actions.

minds_eye_fact.label: Mind's Eye
minds_eye_fact.summary: Grounded language model reasoning through simulation of the environment (p. 24).

world_model_planning_fact.label: Planning with World Models
world_model_planning_fact.summary: The thesis that reasoning with a language model is equivalent to planning with a world model (p. 22).

cognitive_architectures.label: Cognitive Architectures
cognitive_architectures.summary: Computational frameworks intended to model the overall structure of human intelligence.

soar_architecture.label: Soar Cognitive Architecture
soar_architecture.summary: A symbolic architecture for general intelligence focusing on goal-driven behavior and chunking.

soar_chunking_fact.label: Chunking in Soar
soar_chunking_fact.summary: A learning mechanism in Soar that compresses repeated sequences of problem-solving into a single rule (p. 25).

soar_rl_fact.label: Soar-RL
soar_rl_fact.summary: The integration of Reinforcement Learning into the Soar architecture (p. 26).

soar_robotics_fact.label: Cognitive Robotics
soar_robotics_fact.summary: Application of Soar to robotic control and goal-oriented task learning (p. 25).

cognitive_theories.label: Theories of Human Cognition
cognitive_theories.summary: Theoretical foundations for artificial intelligence based on human cognitive limits and processes.

comp_rationality_fact.label: Computational Rationality
comp_rationality_fact.summary: A paradigm suggesting intelligence is the optimal use of limited computational resources (p. 22).

resource_rationality_fact.label: Resource-Rational Analysis
resource_rationality_fact.summary: Understanding human cognition as the optimal use of limited computational resources (p. 24).

physical_symbol_fact.label: Physical Symbol System Hypothesis
physical_symbol_fact.summary: The theory that a physical symbol system has the necessary and sufficient means for general intelligent action (p. 26).

augmented_intelligence.label: Augmented Intelligence
augmented_intelligence.summary: Extending the capabilities of LLMs through external tools, memory, and retrieval systems.

tool_use.label: Tool-Augmented Language Models (TALMs)
tool_use.summary: The ability of LLMs to call external APIs or software tools to solve problems.

toolformer_fact.label: Toolformer
toolformer_fact.summary: An LLM that learns to use tools (like calculators or search engines) autonomously through self-supervised learning (p. 28).

toolllm_fact.label: ToolLLM
toolllm_fact.summary: A system facilitating LLMs to master thousands of real-world APIs (p. 28).

gentopia_fact.label: Gentopia
gentopia_fact.summary: A collaborative platform for tool-augmented LLMs (p. 30).

rag_systems.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
rag_systems.summary: Systems that retrieve relevant documents from a database to provide context for LLM generation.

rag_pretraining_fact.label: Retrieval Augmented Pre-training
rag_pretraining_fact.summary: Integrating retrieval mechanisms directly into the pre-training phase of a language model (p. 22).

llamaindex_fact.label: LlamaIndex
llamaindex_fact.summary: A data framework for connecting custom data sources to LLMs (p. 24).

dense_retrieval_fact.label: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval
dense_retrieval_fact.summary: Using contrastive learning to improve the retrieval of relevant information for LLMs (p. 23).

language_to_action.label: Language-to-Action Mapping
language_to_action.summary: Converting high-level linguistic instructions into low-level robot control commands.

code_as_policies_fact.label: Code as Policies
code_as_policies_fact.summary: Using LLMs to generate code (e.g., Python) that serves as a policy for robotic control (p. 24).

instruct2act_fact.label: Instruct2Act
instruct2act_fact.summary: Mapping multi-modal instructions to robotic actions using LLMs (p. 23).

embodied_reasoning.label: Embodied Reasoning
embodied_reasoning.summary: The ability of an agent to reason about its physical environment and refine its plans based on feedback.

inner_monologue_fact.label: Inner Monologue
inner_monologue_fact.summary: A framework for embodied reasoning through planning and continuous feedback from the environment (p. 23).

progprompt_fact.label: ProgPrompt
progprompt_fact.summary: Generating situated robot task plans via LLMs through programmatic prompting (p. 28).

robotic_systems.label: Robotic Operating Systems
robotic_systems.summary: The software infrastructure used to implement embodied agents.

ros2_fact.label: ROS 2 (Robot Operating System)
ros2_fact.summary: The industry-standard middleware for building robotic applications (p. 25).

learning_alignment.label: Learning and Alignment
learning_alignment.summary: Methods for improving LLM performance and ensuring their outputs align with human values.

reinforcement_learning.label: Reinforcement Learning (RL)
reinforcement_learning.summary: Learning optimal behaviors through trial and error and reward maximization.

sutton_barto_fact.label: Sutton & Barto RL
sutton_barto_fact.summary: The foundational theoretical framework for reinforcement learning (p. 28).

imitation_learning_fact.label: Imitation Learning
imitation_learning_fact.summary: A method of learning a policy by mimicking expert demonstrations (p. 23).

self_improvement.label: Self-Improvement Mechanisms
self_improvement.summary: Algorithms allowing models to improve their own reasoning or performance without new human data.

star_fact.label: STaR (Self-Taught Reasoner)
star_fact.summary: A bootstrapping technique where a model generates reasoning chains, filters for correct ones, and fine-tunes on them (p. 31).

self_refine_fact.label: Self-Refine
self_refine_fact.summary: An iterative process where a model generates an output, provides self-feedback, and refines the output (p. 25).

ethics_alignment.label: Ethics, Bias, and Moral Alignment
ethics_alignment.summary: Ensuring LLMs operate within human moral bounds and are free from systemic bias.

moral_self_correction_fact.label: Moral Self-Correction
moral_self_correction_fact.summary: The capacity of LLMs to identify and correct their own moral errors when prompted (p. 22).

social_bias_fact.label: Social Bias Tracking
social_bias_fact.summary: Tracking how political biases in pre-training data lead to unfair NLP models (p. 22).

socially_aligned_fact.label: Socially Aligned Models
socially_aligned_fact.summary: Training language models to behave according to human social norms within simulated societies (p. 24).
